preferences.cache_retention_hint: This cache holds downloaded DICOM studies and may contain patient information; SonoForge does not encrypt it. Use OS or volume encryption for at-rest protection. One running app enforces a 20 GiB write-admission limit; over-limit downloads are rejected without deleting sessions. Concurrent app instances sharing this cache are not coordinated. Sessions older than 7 days are removed at startup. The open study is kept when clearing here. Disable normal-exit cleanup only if you need the cache between launches; data then remains until cleared or aged out.

persistence.title: Saved measurements
persistence.privacy: Medical data stays on this device until explicitly deleted, separately from the DICOM cache. Files are not encrypted by SonoForge. Protect the OS account and volume; exports may contain patient data.
persistence.toggle_hint: The setting applies immediately: enabling starts saving in the current session; when disabling, the app asks about unsaved changes. On by default in the full build; off in Presenter. Records are kept until explicitly deleted.
persistence.notice_text: Measurements and height/weight are saved automatically on this computer (in the application data folder), separately from the DICOM cache, and stay there until explicitly deleted. The files are not encrypted — protect your account and disk; this is not a backup of the study. To turn it off or delete records: Settings → Other → Saved measurements.
persistence.conflict_text: An open study already has saved measurements that were not loaded in this session. Load them (current session measurements will be replaced) or keep the current ones (the saved record will be overwritten on the next save)?
persistence.disable_dirty_text: There are unsaved changes. Save them before turning autosave off?
persistence.disable_blocked: Could not finish saving — autosave stays enabled. Try turning it off later or use the saved-measurements manager.
persistence.partial: Partial restore: some source clips are missing
persistence.error: Measurements not saved/restored ({code}). RAM changes are retained. Open Settings → Saved measurements to retry or export.
persistence.blocked_navigation: Some measurements are not saved. Opening another study or closing was cancelled. Retry or export in Settings → Saved measurements.

calc.input.hr: Heart rate during the LVOT VTI recording
calc.input.bsa: Body surface area (Du Bois from height and weight by default)
calc.output.ava_vmax: Aortic valve area, simplified continuity equation (Vmax)
calc.assumptions.stroke_volume: Circular LVOT; diameter and the PW VTI sample at the same level (3–10 mm below the valve); the diameter error is squared. Cardiac output needs the heart rate during the VTI recording.
calc.assumptions.aortic_valve_area: Circular LVOT; LVOT VTI and Vmax by PW, AV by CW along the highest-velocity jet; same rhythm and comparable beats. The Vmax form ignores the flow profile. DVI does not depend on the LVOT diameter.
calc.source.dicom: DICOM HeartRate of the LVOT VTI clip
calc.source.derived_bsa: from height and weight, Du Bois
calc.warning.out_of_range: {label} outside the usual range {low}–{high} {unit} — check the measurement
calc.warning.dvi_above_one: LVOT flow exceeds AV flow (DVI > 1) — labels or modes are probably swapped (LVOT is PW, AV is CW)
calc.warning.ava_methods_diverge: AVA by VTI and by Vmax differ by {percent}% — check that LVOT and AV signals come from comparable beats
calc.ruo: Calculations are for reference only (RUO, research use only): verify the inputs; missing values are never replaced by typical ones.
calc.input.pisa_r_mr: Mitral regurgitation PISA radius — "PISA MR" caliper on a colour frame, from the aliasing line to the orifice
calc.input.va_mr: Aliasing (Nyquist) velocity of the colour scale towards the MR jet when the PISA is measured
calc.input.mr_vmax: Peak velocity of the MR jet (CW)
calc.input.mr_vti: Velocity-time integral of the MR jet (CW)
calc.input.pisa_r_ar: Aortic regurgitation PISA radius — "PISA AR" caliper on a colour frame
calc.input.va_ar: Aliasing (Nyquist) velocity of the colour scale towards the AR jet when the PISA is measured
calc.input.ar_vmax: Peak velocity of the AR jet (CW)
calc.input.ar_vti: Velocity-time integral of the AR jet (CW)
calc.source.manual_only.va_mr: type it in: aliasing velocity from the scanner colour scale
calc.source.manual_only.va_ar: type it in: aliasing velocity from the scanner colour scale
calc.assumptions.pisa_mr: Hemispheric isovelocity shell over a flat orifice; radius at the peak MR velocity (mid-systole), colour baseline shifted towards the jet, Va is the aliasing velocity of that scale; Vmax and VTI by CW along the same jet. Holosystolic jet: late-systolic or multiple jets and non-circular (slit-like) orifices make EROA over- or underestimated. RF uses RVol plus the LVOT stroke volume and assumes no significant aortic regurgitation. Primary and secondary MR have different grades.
calc.assumptions.pisa_ar: Hemispheric isovelocity shell over a flat orifice; radius in early diastole, colour baseline shifted towards the jet, Va is the aliasing velocity of that scale; Vmax and VTI by CW along the same jet. Harder than for MR (eccentric jets, orifice hidden by the cusps); unreliable with an eccentric jet. RF is relative to the LVOT stroke volume, which already contains the regurgitant volume.
calc.warning.rf_above_100: Regurgitant fraction {percent}% > 100 % — the regurgitant volume exceeds the LVOT stroke volume: check the PISA radius, Va, the jet VTI and the LVOT inputs
constructor.meta.note_placeholder: Caveat to the gradations (shown under them)...
calc.input.pisa_r_ms: PISA radius in mitral stenosis — “PISA MS” caliper on a colour frame (atrial side), from the aliasing line to the orifice
calc.input.va_ms: Aliasing (Nyquist) velocity of the colour scale towards the transmitral flow when measuring PISA
calc.input.ms_angle: Angle α between the mitral leaflets on the atrial side (PISA funnel)
calc.input.rvot_d: RVOT diameter at the RVOT VTI PW sample site (below the pulmonary valve) — “RVOTd” caliper
calc.input.rap: Right atrial pressure estimated from IVC size and collapse
calc.input.orifice_d: Diameter of any circular orifice (pulmonary annulus, conduit, etc.)
calc.source.manual_only.va_ms: type it in: aliasing velocity from the scanner colour scale
calc.source.manual_only.ms_angle: type it in: angle between the leaflets on the colour frame
calc.source.manual_only.rap: type it in: 3, 8 or 15 mmHg from the IVC (see the reference)
calc.output.mva_pht: Mitral valve area by pressure half-time (Hatle)
calc.output.mva_pisa: Mitral valve area by PISA with angle correction
calc.output.tr_pg: RV–RA systolic gradient from tricuspid regurgitation
calc.output.mpap_pasp: Mean PA pressure from systolic PA pressure (Chemla)
calc.output.mpap_at: Mean PA pressure from RVOT acceleration time (Mahan)
calc.output.qp: Pulmonary flow per beat (RVOT stroke volume)
calc.output.qs: Systemic flow per beat (LVOT stroke volume)
calc.output.area_d: Area of a circular orifice of diameter D
calc.assumptions.mitral_valve_area: PHT: the constant 220 is empirical; not valid right after commissurotomy (first 72 h), with significant aortic regurgitation, abnormal LV/LA compliance or for prostheses; in atrial fibrillation average several beats and avoid short cycles. PISA: hemispheric shell corrected for the angle α between the leaflets; colour baseline shifted towards the flow, Va is the aliasing velocity of that scale, Vmax is the peak transmitral CW velocity.
calc.assumptions.pulmonary_pressure: PASP = 4·V² + RAP assumes no RVOT obstruction or pulmonary stenosis; an incomplete TR envelope underestimates it. RAP is never assumed — enter it from the IVC. mPAP (Chemla) is derived from PASP, mPAP (Mahan) from the RVOT acceleration time (unreliable outside HR 60–100). The Abbas PVR formula was validated up to about 8 WU and underestimates higher resistance. Echocardiography estimates the probability of PH; it does not replace catheterisation.
calc.assumptions.qp_qs: RVOT and LVOT are assumed circular; each diameter at its own PW sample site, the diameter error enters squared (especially for the RVOT). No significant pulmonary or aortic regurgitation, one rhythm and comparable beats. Suited to atrial and ventricular level shunts; in PDA the ratio is reversed (Qp is measured in the LVOT).
calc.assumptions.teichholz: Volumes from a single linear dimension (prolate ellipsoid model): diameters perpendicular to the LV long axis at the mitral leaflet tips, at end-diastole and end-systole. Not valid with regional wall-motion abnormalities or distorted LV geometry. ASE/EACVI 2015 do not recommend linear methods for EF — biplane Simpson is preferred; the EF gradations in the reference refer to Simpson.
calc.assumptions.orifice_area: The orifice is assumed circular: area = π·(D/2)². The diameter error enters squared (1 mm at D = 2 cm is about 10 % of the area). LVOT and RVOT are often oval — a single-diameter area under- or overestimates the true one.
calc.warning.lvesd_not_below_lvedd: LVESD is not smaller than LVEDD — labels or cardiac phases are probably swapped; EF, FS and SV are not calculated
calc.input.mr_dpdt_dt: Time for the MR jet to rise from 1 to 3 m/s (CW) — "MR dP/dt" interval on the ascending limb
calc.input.tr_dpdt_dt: Time for the TR jet to rise from 1 to 2 m/s (CW) — "TR dP/dt" interval on the ascending limb
calc.output.lv_dpdt: LV rate of pressure rise (dP/dt) from the MR jet
calc.output.rv_dpdt: RV rate of pressure rise (dP/dt) from the TR jet
calc.title.dpdt: LV and RV dP/dt (from regurgitant jets)
calc.assumptions.dpdt: By the simplified Bernoulli equation the rise from 1 to 3 m/s corresponds to a 32 mmHg pressure rise (LV) and from 1 to 2 m/s to 12 mmHg (RV); dP/dt = ΔP/Δt is the mean over that interval. It needs a clear CW envelope of the regurgitant jet at a fast sweep (100–200 mm/s), with the marks placed exactly at 1 and 3 (or 2) m/s. Not valid with an eccentric or incompletely recorded jet or with acute severe regurgitation; the index depends on preload and afterload.
